inspection_summary: Inspected all 937 frozen logical lines (914 LF-delimited physical lines plus 23 form-feed page boundaries). The normalized text preserves the paper's prose-level proof architecture but loses or scrambles much of the displayed mathematics: most equations in Sections 2-4, including the exact statements of Theorems 1-3, are not transcription-safe. Six conservative method units are recoverable from explicit prose. Lines 884-937 are journal-issue contents material rather than a continuation of the article: lines 884-903 are a badly OCRed contents scan and lines 909-937 repeat the contents more cleanly; neither is mathematical source depth.

sections_inspected.label: Journal cover, repeated article title, and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Editorial front matter plus an abstract announcing integral families for integer zeta values; example displays are extraction-damaged.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Places the work among earlier log-sine and log-sinh evaluations and announces parity-indexed generalizations and cross-family relations.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Representation of zeta(n) by log-sinh integrals
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Rewrites exponential kernels hyperbolically, evaluates auxiliary integral families through substitutions and integration by parts, and states odd/even zeta representation formulas whose exact displays are mostly lost.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Representation of zeta(n) by log-sine integrals
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses a complex contour substitution and real/imaginary projections to derive log-sine moment identities involving zeta, a Dirichlet function, Bernoulli numbers, and Euler numbers; exact formulas are heavily degraded.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Relations with central-binomial series
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds iterated-integral generating functions from arcsine and inverse-hyperbolic-sine series to connect central-binomial sums with log-sine and log-sinh moments.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic, funding, affiliation, and contact information only.

accepted_units.title: Parity-split program for representing integer zeta values by logarithmic moments
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction explicitly organizes prior isolated log-sine and log-sinh evaluations into two general tasks: rederive odd zeta representations, add an even analogue, prove general log-sine formulas, and relate the circular and hyperbolic integral families. This supplies the source's conceptual comparison even though the displayed target formulas are damaged.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit preserves the literature contrast and section roadmap; exact equations (1.1)-(1.9) are not recoverable from this span and must not be inferred.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the prose reliably identifies parity and function families, but the concrete integral identities and constants are largely absent or scrambled.

accepted_units.title: Exponential denominators rewritten as log-sinh kernels
accepted_units.why_material: The visible identity factoring an exponential difference through a hyperbolic sine explains why substitutions in a standard zeta-integral kernel generate powers of log(2 sinh(theta/2)). The special choice of an algebraic endpoint then creates paired auxiliary integrals to be evaluated.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the section setup, the exponential-to-sinh factorization, the analogous step, auxiliary definitions, and specialization. Several defining displays are incomplete, so the unit records only the representation change and setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: line 143 preserves the core factorization semantically, but equations (2.1)-(2.5), the exact endpoint, and the definitions of the auxiliary functions require PDF recovery.

accepted_units.title: Auxiliary-integral evaluation by reciprocal substitutions, integration by parts, and parity recombination
accepted_units.why_material: The prose documents a reusable evaluation pipeline: evaluate two auxiliary families, transform their integrals by substitutions, reduce a remaining logarithmic integral by integration by parts, derive separate even and odd relations, and substitute those relations back into the original pair. This is the mechanism leading to the Section 2 representation theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: The sequence of operations is explicit at lines 167, 189, 226, 246, 264, 280, and 293, but the intervening equations are badly fragmented. Treat this as method architecture, not as an executable derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: definitions, signs, coefficients, limits, and recurrences in equations (2.6)-(2.12) are not transcription-safe.

accepted_units.title: A complex contour identity converted into log-sine moment families
accepted_units.why_material: The source defines B(theta)=log(2 sin(theta/2)), integrates along a specified unit-circle arc, applies a complex affine substitution, and splits the result into real-variable integrals. Taking real and imaginary parts at opposite parity choices, then invoking Bernoulli- and Euler-number coefficient identities, is the stated route to the two general log-sine theorem families.
accepted_units.context_note: The contour, path endpoints, substitution, and projection steps are prose-visible. The unit intentionally does not reproduce equations (3.1)-(3.15) or Theorems 2-3 because their displays are extensively lost.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the exact contour integrand, the auxiliary Dirichlet function, all coefficients, and both theorem statements need direct PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Iterated integration of the arcsine series produces log-sine moment identities
accepted_units.why_material: Starting from the central-binomial expansion of arcsin(x)/x, the source integrates and differentiates to obtain related series, then constructs a polylogarithm-like hierarchy K_m(x). Repeated integration by parts and the substitution x=sin(theta/2) turn the hierarchy into integrals of powers of log(2x), hence log-sine moments.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction sequence and substitutions are explicit despite missing coefficients. The endpoint specializations following line 730 are excluded because their formulas are blank.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the iterative mechanism is readable, but equations (4.1)-(4.4) and exact central-binomial weights require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Imaginary substitution creates the inverse-hyperbolic-sine companion hierarchy
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing x by ix in the arcsine identities produces inverse-hyperbolic-sine series. The source builds an analogous F_m hierarchy and, after integration by parts, connects the resulting central-binomial sums to log-sinh moments. This explains structurally why the circular and hyperbolic integral families occur in parallel.
accepted_units.context_note: Relies on the preceding arcsine construction in u05. The prose at lines 755, 769, 779, 788, 797, and 805 supports the sequence, while the displayed identities remain incomplete.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: equations (4.11)-(4.18), the exact signs, weights, endpoint, and resulting integral formula must be recovered from the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Parity is extracted by changing representation before evaluating moments
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source repeatedly changes an integral kernel into a logarithmic representation and then separates even and odd index families through paired auxiliary identities or real/imaginary projections, rather than evaluating each integer zeta value independently.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact parity formulas and coefficients are unavailable in the normalized extraction, so this synthesis records strategy only.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Circular and hyperbolic logarithmic moments form parallel constructions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Log-sinh moments arise from exponential or inverse-hyperbolic-sine representations, while log-sine moments arise from unit-circle or arcsine representations; analytic substitution links the two families at the level of generating constructions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source's exact domains, endpoints, branch conventions, and constants require PDF recovery.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Iterated-integral hierarchies bridge coefficient series to logarithmic moments
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Applying repeated integration and integration by parts to arcsine/asinh coefficient series raises logarithmic powers and converts central-binomial sums into trigonometric or hyperbolic logarithmic moments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Because equations (4.1)-(4.18) are incomplete, the synthesis cannot safely state the weights or normalization.
